activity.name: Bash
activity.arg:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
c0008: the grid grows and shrinks

An arrow key adds a row or a column at the edge it points at, and Shift with an
arrow takes that edge away again. `Edge::Top` is row 0 - the first line of the
layout, which is what an author sees at the top of the screen under both
cameras; `cell_to_world` calls the same row the bottom one because it works in
world coordinates, where z grows towards the player, and the enum now says so.
Row 0's world position is fixed, so a grid always grows towards the paddle
whichever end the row is added at - but every cell that is kept keeps its token,
which is what the card asks for.

`grow`, `shrink` and `set_cell` are three lines each on top of one pair of
helpers: `slot_grid` reads a layout as rows of slots squared up to the widest
one, `write_grid` writes them back. So there is a single place a ragged grid is
padded out, and `interpret_grid`'s first-line column count stays true of every
row after a resize.

Undo is `c0011`'s and depends on this card, so removing an edge with blocks on it
warns first. An empty edge costs nothing and goes on the first press; an edge
with blocks on it is named and counted, in orange at the bottom of the screen and
in the log, with the doomed cells outlined on the grid - and the same press again
means it. Painting, growing, asking after another edge or leaving the editor all
drop the warning, because it counted the level as it stood.

A grid keeps its last row and column, and stops growing where the editor could no
longer show it whole - 13 x 16 for the shipped gap, against a widest shipped level
of 11. Whether a grid that wide is one a ball can reach every cell of is `c0012`'s
to warn about.

26 new tests, 132 green, build clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1; git show --stat --format="" HEAD
